summary: Luca Maria Olivieri is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who earned his doctorate from the Free University of Berlin. He directed the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East around 2014 and taught at Ca' Foscari University of Venice (2020–2021).

Lucia Dolce works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She has held posts at SOAS University of London as Lecturer in Japanese Religions (attested 2003–2007) and associate professor (attested 2015), and is attested at Minobusan University in 2026.
Lucia Galli is a scholar of Tibetology who completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford and held a post there.

Lucian Scherman was an Indologist who studied at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and earned his doctorate at Munich under Ernst Kuhn. He served as a professor at the University of Munich (c. 1893–1933) and headed the Museum Fünf Kontinente from 1907.

Luciano Petech was a scholar of Tibetology and history who studied under Giuseppe Tucci. He served as Lector in Italian at the University of Allahabad (1938–1946) and held the Chair of History of Eastern Asia at Sapienza University of Rome (1955–1984).

Lucien Lévy-Bruhl was a French scholar of philosophy and religion who studied at the École Normale Supérieure and the Sorbonne. He founded the Institut d'ethnologie and held a post at the University of Paris from circa 1899 to 1927.

Lucien Tesnière was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and attended the University of Paris, University of Leipzig, and ENLOV. He held academic posts at the universities of Ljubljana (c. 1920–1924), Strasbourg (1924–1937), and Montpellier (1937).
Lucy Annette Jones is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Rice University under the supervision of Anne Carolyn Klein and Edith Wyschogrod.

Ludo Rocher was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Ghent University and SOAS under scholars including Adriaan Scharpé and Jan Gonda. He taught at the Université libre de Bruxelles (1959–1967) and was a professor and chair at the University of Pennsylvania (1966–2002).

Ludwig Alsdorf was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctorates under Walther Schubring and Heinrich Lüders. He held posts at Allahabad, Münster, and Humboldt University of Berlin before holding the chair of Indian history and culture at Hamburg (1950–1972).

Ludwig Diestel was a scholar of religion who studied under Heinrich Ewald. He held academic posts at the universities of Greifswald (c. 1858–1862), Bonn (c. 1862–1867), Jena (c. 1867–1872), and Tübingen (c. 1872–1879).

Ludwig Heller was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Kielhorn at Göttingen and habilitated at Greifswald. He held posts at the Royal Library of Berlin (1893), the University of Greifswald (1904), and the University of Tartu (1918).

Ludwig Lange was a scholar in linguistics and archaeology who studied under Theodor Benfey at Göttingen and at Leipzig. He served as professor of classical philology at Charles University, the University of Giessen, and the University of Leipzig, where he was also rector.

Ludwig Ross was an archaeologist who studied at Kiel University. He held academic posts at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens from 1837 to 1843 and at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1845 to 1859.

Ludwig Wittgenstein was a philosopher who studied at Technische Hochschule Berlin, Manchester, and Cambridge, earning his PhD there in 1929. He served as a lecturer, fellow, and professor of philosophy at the University of Cambridge between 1929 and 1947.
Ludwik Skurzak was an Indologist who studied under Stanisław Schayer. He later served as a lecturer at the University of Breslau.
Luigi Suali was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Bologna and under Hermann Jacobi. He held an academic post at the University of Pavia from circa 1907 to 1939.

Luis Oscar Gómez was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Stanley Insler and completed doctoral degrees at Yale and Michigan. He held professorial and chair positions at the University of Michigan and served as Academic Director at Mangalam Research Center.

Luise Hercus was an Indologist and linguist who studied at St Anne's College and Australian National University. She taught at St Anne's College, held a fellowship at the University of Adelaide, and was a Sanskrit lecturer at Australian National University (c. 1969–1991).
Lungten Dubgyur is a Tibetology scholar who completed degrees at Sherubtse College, Government Law College in Mumbai (LL.B), and the University of Edinburgh (LL.M).
